title: Operational Horizon: Sprint Gating & Skill Rotation Protocol
creator: Anika Rao
description: Design a lightweight, repeatable protocol for gating sprint commitments and rotating specialist skills across cycles. Goal: reduce mid-cycle emergency reassignments, make scope cuts predictable, and preserve delivery velocity for critical platform work. This protocol sits between long-horizon planning and daily standups: it defines gating thresholds (capacity, risk score, unblock probability), who owns gating decisions, and a formal skill-rotation / shadowing calendar for cross-training.
acceptance_criteria: A clear gating checklist documented and adopted by two product teams and one infra team by 2026-03-29
Automated capacity signal (headcount x availability) integrated into the cycle planning doc and used in at least one pre-commit review
Skill rotation runbook created with at least 4 cross-shadowing pairs scheduled and a simple sign-up flow
One simulated scope-cut exercise executed in the cycle rehearsal with time-to-decision under 48 hours
decisions: Gating owner will be the cycle lead (PM) with verification from ENG tech lead and a design/UX representative for customer-facing changes
Capacity threshold set to 80% committed FTE-equivalent for stretch scope; anything beyond requires explicit reserve lane or approved contingency
Triage risk scoring adopts three vectors: complexity (1-5), external dependency (1-5), and rollback difficulty (1-5); total >=12 triggers canary-only/deferral discussion
Skill rotations will be 2-week shadow blocks with a 1-week buffer in between; volunteers first, then assigned by manager if slots unfilled
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Drafted initial gating checklist; solicited feedback from infra-eng and two PMs; identified missing capacity signal integration
2026-03-04: Eng leads requested a simpler risk scoring UI; removed low-value fields to reduce friction
2026-03-06: Held 45m sync with Design to align on customer-impact framing for scope cuts; agreed to require example rollback playbook for any UI change >2 complexity
2026-03-08: Pilot sign-up sheet for skill rotations deployed; first four volunteers recorded; updated estimate to 5 points
reviewers_feedback: Maya Thompson (Eng): 'Keep gating fast — checkbox checklist and automatic capacity calc required, otherwise it will be avoided.'
Luca Fernandez (Design): 'Scope-cut rationale must include a customer journey snippet to ensure we don't inadvertently break flows.'
Priya Kapoor (Head of PM): 'Consider a soft-freeze window definition to protect cross-team integrations during critical launches.'
next_actions: Finalize gating checklist and add to Cycle kickoff doc by 2026-03-12
Hook capacity calculation into the planning spreadsheet (HR availability x planned allocation) — ENG to provide headcount API by 2026-03-15
Run a simulated scope-cut tabletop exercise in the Cycle Rehearsal on 2026-03-22
Publish a one-page skill-rotation sign-up and manager assignment flow; communicate in weekly all-PM on 2026-03-10
notes: Trade-offs: stricter gates reduce scope churn but can push work to later cycles, increasing lead time; prefer a hybrid with small dedicated contingency for infra
Operational constraints: managers must agree to backfill shadowed headcount for at least 1 sprint, else rotation deferred
Escalation: if gating decision cannot be reached within 48 hours the default is 'defer non-blocking scope' and route to Head of PM for tie-break
Measurement: track number of mid-cycle reassignments, average time to scope-cut decision, and % of committed scope delivered per cycle; baseline metrics to be captured during pilot
